2027-02-21.title: Second Sunday of Lent
readings: The sacrifice of our father Abraham
I will walk before the Lord, in the land of the living
God did not spare his own Son
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!
2027-02-21.alt: Year B. The memorial of St Peter Damian is not kept this year because it falls on Sunday. No Gloria. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-21.verse: Then a cloud overshadowed them, and from the cloud there came a voice, “This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!”
theo: Every Second Sunday of Lent leads us up the mountain of the Transfiguration, and in Year B the Church sets beside it the hardest story in Genesis. “After these things God tested Abraham.” He calls him by name, and Abraham answers as the saints always answer: “Here I am.” Then the terrible command: “Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering.” Each phrase tightens the knot: your son, your only son, whom you love. Isaac is the child of the promise, the one through whom all nations are to be blessed. Abraham is asked to give back to God the very gift God gave him. He goes, he builds the altar, he binds his son and lifts the knife. Then the angel calls: “Abraham, Abraham!… Do not lay your hand on the boy… for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.” A ram caught in a thicket takes Isaac's place. God never wanted the death of Isaac. He wanted Abraham's whole heart, and he received it.

St Paul reads this story in the light of Calvary. “He who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else?” Paul is echoing Genesis on purpose. What God spared Abraham, he did not spare himself. On Moriah the son was released and a substitute was found; on Golgotha there was no substitute, because the Son himself is the Lamb. The Fathers loved to point out that Isaac carried the wood of the sacrifice up the hill, as Jesus would carry his cross. And Abraham's words to his son, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering”, find their full meaning at the Jordan when John points to Jesus: here is the Lamb of God. That is why Paul can ask with such confidence: “If God is for us, who is against us?… Who is to condemn? It is Christ Jesus, who died, yes, who was raised, who is at the right hand of God, who indeed intercedes for us.”

Then Mark takes us up “a high mountain apart”. Jesus has just told the disciples that the Son of Man must suffer, be rejected and be killed. Now, for a moment, Peter, James and John see who is walking towards that death. “He was transfigured before them, and his clothes became dazzling white, such as no one on earth could bleach them.” Moses and Elijah, the Law and the Prophets, talk with him. Peter, terrified and delighted, wants to build three dwellings and stay. But a cloud overshadows them, and the Father's voice speaks the words Abraham might have spoken over Isaac: “This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!” When they look again, “they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus.” The vision passes; Jesus remains. Coming down, he tells them to keep silence “until after the Son of Man had risen from the dead”. The glory of the mountain is given to carry them through the darkness of the cross. Lent is the same: a climb with Jesus towards Jerusalem, sustained by moments of light, and above all by the command to listen to him.
conn: Later tradition identified the mountain of Isaac's binding with the Temple mount in Jerusalem, where Solomon built the house of the Lord (2 Chronicles 3:1).
Your only son, whom you love.
The Greek Old Testament uses agapētos, beloved, for Isaac (Genesis 22:2); the Father's voice in Mark 9:7 calls Jesus ho agapētos, the Beloved.
From the second century, Christian writers saw Isaac carrying the wood up the hill as a figure of Christ carrying his cross.
They stand for the Law and the Prophets; both met God on the mountain, Sinai and Horeb, and both heard him in a cloud or a still sound.
Peter's booths recall the Feast of Tabernacles, when Israel lived in tents to remember the desert and to hope for the days of the Messiah.
Since at least the fourth century Christian tradition has placed the Transfiguration on Tabor in Galilee, where the Basilica of the Transfiguration now stands.
altar: At the consecration the priest takes the bread and wine and speaks the words of the Son who was not spared. The Father gives us his Beloved in the Eucharist, as Paul says: will he not with him also give us everything else?
The glory seen on the mountain is hidden under the forms of bread and wine. We cannot see it, but we listen to him and believe: this is my Body, this is my Blood.
outline: Ask: what is the most precious gift you have, and could you give it back to God?
Your son, your only son, whom you love.
The ram, the Lamb, the Son not spared.
Glory for the road to the cross.
Isaac carrying the wood up the hill; Jesus carrying the cross.
“This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!”
live: Offer to God in prayer the person or thing you love most, and trust him with it.
Spend ten minutes each day this week with the Gospel, asking: Lord, what are you saying to me?
Make a holy hour before the Blessed Sacrament this week.
Accept one daily burden this week without complaining, united with Jesus on the way to Calvary.
fathers: The chief purpose of the Transfiguration was to remove the scandal of the cross from the hearts of the disciples, so that the humiliation of his chosen Passion would not shake the faith of those to whom the glory of his hidden dignity had been revealed.

Come down, Peter. You wanted to rest on the mountain; come down and preach the word, labour, suffer. Life came down to be slain, Bread came down to be hungry, the Way came down to grow weary on the way, and you refuse to labour?

Isaac, bound and silent on the wood, was a figure of Christ who was to suffer; yet Isaac was set free, while Christ suffered in truth, and the ram caught in the thicket foreshadowed the Lord crowned with thorns.
magis: The Transfiguration: a foretaste of the Kingdom, given to strengthen the apostles before the Passion.
Abraham's prayer and the testing of his faith; God himself will provide the lamb.
God did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all.
The transfigured Christ as the icon of every life given wholly to God.
Benedict XVI, Jesus of Nazareth I, ch. 9
The Transfiguration read in the light of the Feast of Tabernacles and of the Exodus that Jesus was to accomplish in Jerusalem.
saints: St Peter Damian (not kept this year)
Orphaned as a boy and set to herd pigs, he became a Camaldolese monk, a fearless reformer, Cardinal-Bishop of Ostia and Doctor of the Church (1007–1072).
22 Feb: Chair of St Peter (feast). 23 Feb: St Polycarp (commemoration). 24–27 Feb: Lenten weekdays. 28 Feb: Third Sunday of Lent.
2027-02-21.prayer: O God, who have commanded us to listen to your beloved Son, be pleased, we pray, to nourish us inwardly by your word, that, with spiritual sight made pure, we may rejoice to behold your glory. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, beloved Son of the Father, you were transfigured on the mountain and then went down to Jerusalem to give your life for us. Give us Abraham's trust to offer you what we love most, open our ears to listen to you, and let the light of your glory carry us through every cross to Easter. Amen.

quick: Abraham is ready to give God his only son, and God provides a ram instead.

2027-02-21.action: Spend ten minutes each day this week listening to Jesus in the Gospel.
2027-02-21.question: What is the Isaac in my life that God is asking me to trust to him?
catechism: Abraham's faith tested; God provides the lamb.
God did not spare his own Son.
kidsaint: When he was a little boy, his mother and father died, and he was sent to look after pigs. One day he found a coin. He was very poor, but instead of buying something for himself, he gave it to a priest to pray at Mass for his father. Later he became a great saint and a cardinal. Lesson: even when we have little, we can give it to God!
2027-02-21.special: Second Sunday of Lent. St Peter Damian not kept this year.
term: Hebrew for “binding”: the Jewish name for the story of Abraham binding Isaac on Mount Moriah (Genesis 22), which Christians read as a figure of the sacrifice of Christ.

family.explain: Jesus took three friends up a high mountain. Suddenly his face and clothes shone bright white! Moses and Elijah were there. Then God the Father spoke from a cloud: This is my Son, whom I love. Listen to him!
family.intention: We pray for everyone who finds it hard to listen to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we listen to Jesus better as a family this Lent?”

illus: A widow in Changanassery had only one son, an engineer with a good job. One day he told her he wanted to become a priest and go as a missionary to Africa. She cried for a week. Then, on a Sunday when this reading from Genesis was proclaimed, she went to the parish priest and said: I have been holding my Isaac too tightly. At his ordination she gave him her hands to anoint first. She says now that she has never felt so close to her son as since the day she gave him back.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, beloved Son of the Father, lead us up the mountain, show us your glory, and teach us to listen to you. Amen.
share: Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love (Genesis 22:2). What is God asking me to entrust to him?
He who did not withhold his own Son (Romans 8:32). Do I believe God will give me everything with him?
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him! (Mark 9:7). How do I listen to Jesus?
pm.resp: I will walk before the Lord, in the land of the living.
interc: For parents who have lost a child, and for those who have given their children to God.
For all who are tested in faith.
For the elect preparing for baptism at Easter.
For priests and religious, that their lives may reflect the transfigured Christ.
For our group, that we may listen to Jesus and follow him to the cross.
pm.close: Father, you commanded us to listen to your beloved Son. Open our ears and our hearts, and let his glory sustain us on the way to Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, after these things God tested Abraham. He said, take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love… and offer him there as a burnt offering (Genesis 22:1–2). Every word of that command is heavy. Isaac was the gift of God, the son of the promise.

Abraham went. He built the altar, laid the wood, bound his son and took the knife. Then the angel called: do not lay your hand on the boy… for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me (Genesis 22:12). God did not want Isaac's death. He wanted Abraham's whole heart.

St Paul looks at Calvary and says: he who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else? (Romans 8:32). What God spared Abraham, he did not spare himself. On Moriah a ram was found; on Golgotha the Son himself is the Lamb.

In the Gospel Jesus leads Peter, James and John up a high mountain, and he was transfigured before them, and his clothes became dazzling white (Mark 9:2–3). They see for a moment the glory of the one who will soon be rejected and crucified.

Then a cloud overshadowed them, and the Father said: this is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him! (Mark 9:7). And suddenly they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus (Mark 9:8). The vision passes; Jesus remains. That is enough.

This Lent, let us offer God our Isaac, whatever we hold too tightly, and trust that he will provide. And let us listen to his Son every day. The light of the mountain will carry us through the cross to Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus took three friends up a mountain, and his clothes became shining white! Then God the Father said: this is my Son, I love him, listen to him!
This week, let us listen to Jesus: read a little bit of the Gospel each day with Mummy or Daddy.

intro: Theme: “This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!”
Abraham's test, the Son not spared, the glory on the mountain, and the one command of the Father.

sub: Your son, your only son, whom you love.
q: He said, “Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I shall show you.”
By faith Abraham, when put to the test, offered up Isaac. He who had received the promises was ready to offer up his only son,
points.apply: Offer to God in prayer the person or thing you hold most tightly.

q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.
He who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else?
points.apply: Thank God each night this week for one thing he has provided.

sub: After the first prediction of the Passion.
Glory for the road to the cross.
q: Moses came down from Mount Sinai. As he came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in his hand, Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And he was transfigured before them, and his clothes became dazzling white, such as no one on earth could bleach them.
points.apply: Spend an hour before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
Then a cloud overshadowed them, and from the cloud there came a voice, “This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!”
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel again each day this week and ask: what is Jesus saying to me?

concl: God did not spare his own Son; with him he gives us everything.
The light of the mountain carries us through the cross; the Father's command is simple: listen to him.
2027-02-21.resolve: Spend ten minutes daily with the Gospel for the rest of Lent.
